newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open firm, LVMH soars.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open firm, LVMH soars.

text.p: The CAC-40 index strengthened at the opening on Monday, buoyed by new opinion polls that appeared to reassure investors about the conservatives' lead over the Socialist party in France's upcoming parliamentary election, traders said.
The drinks sector bubbled higher, with LVMH and Pernod Ricard rising on the news that Britain's Guinness and Grand Met planned to merge.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 17.93 points or 0.68 percent at 2,651.84 at 0812 GMT, after opening up 0.56 percent. The CAC-40 futures contract was up 21 at 2,636 from Friday's close.

LVMH added 2.32 percent to 1,410 francs on turnover of 30 million francs. Traders said LVMH would benefit from a reevaluation of its 14 percent stake in Guinness and the merger with Grand Met could open up new outlets for LVMH brands.
Pernod Ricard rose 2.07 percent to 306.1 in sympathy.
Danone, which has major brewing interests, underperformed with a 0.23 percent rise to 862. The Guinness merger would likely stiffen competition.
TF1 fell 3.55 percent to 570 francs. Its first quarter sales and advertising revenues compared poorly with those of Metropole Television M6, which was down 0.84 percent to 589.
TF1's advertising revenues rose 2.3 percent in the period, compared to a 12.4 percent gain for M6, the urban television channel which relies heavily on imports of U.S. made-for-TV thrillers.

Lagardere held last week's strong gains, rising 1.87 percent to 184.80, as the market bets on the books-to-missiles group winning Thomson-CSF on the strength of its ties with Germany's Dasa and British Aerospace.
Gan gained 2.84 percent to 145, holding last week's rise following confirmation that AGF is in interested in buying Gan's insurance business. AGF was up 0.37 percent at 190.2.
Axa, rose 0.68 percent at 367.5, was among busiest stocks.
Much of the market activity was led by short-covering in the futures pit, with investors staying out of the market.
